## TL;DR

Replaced the Android GitHub Release download path with a maintainer-run publish flow. `just publish-hub-apk` loads the existing signing values from the environment or the untracked `~/.config/repoos-hub/release-signing.env`, builds the release APK with Gradle's configuration cache disabled, verifies its release certificate, rejects debuggable output, generates version and checksum metadata, and uploads the APK and `version.json` to the private `repoos-hub-downloads` R2 bucket. The landing Worker exposes only the two public download URLs. The landing page shows “Coming soon” until metadata is available and includes the version when a release is present.

The Android Actions workflow now builds and tests the debug variant only. The Hub guide, mobile README, root README and release runbook now describe the local publish/update flow. No live APK was built or published, and no Cloudflare account changes or deployment were made.

## Work and rationale

The publisher is a Bun TypeScript script called by a `just` recipe. It reads only the four expected `REPOOS_ANDROID_*` names from the optional config file, without sourcing it as shell code, and gives environment values precedence. It validates all signing values and the keystore path before starting the build. A real publish also checks for `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` before doing expensive work; `--dry-run` skips that requirement and exits after verification and metadata reporting, so it cannot upload. The script does not print credential values. It reuses `mobile/scripts/verify-release-apk.ts` for signer verification, checks `aapt` badging for the debuggable flag, computes APK size and SHA-256, and emits version name, version code, certificate SHA-256 and build time in metadata.

The release build recipe now passes `--no-configuration-cache` to Gradle. Publishing uploads the APK first and the metadata second, making the metadata the final indication that a newly uploaded version is available. The regular landing-site deploy has no deletion step for the R2 bucket, so deploying site assets cannot remove the APK.

The landing Worker binds the private R2 bucket and routes the exact APK and JSON paths through Worker-first routing. The APK response uses Android's package content type and an attachment filename; the JSON has a 60-second public cache. Both routes handle GET and HEAD, reject other methods, and return 404 for missing objects. Other `/downloads/` paths are also 404 and do not read arbitrary bucket keys. The Vue download component fetches the metadata, renders a versioned link only when a valid version name is present, and otherwise renders the requested empty state. The existing Mac download was left intact.

Documentation no longer claims that stable GitHub releases carry an Android APK or recommends browsing older releases as a fallback. It explains maintainer configuration, publishing, dry-run use, certificate verification from `version.json`, and installing an update over the existing app. CI remains useful for Android builds/tests without implying that it signs or attaches a release APK.

## Approaches tried

I first inspected the existing Android Gradle release build, the APK verifier, Worker structure, landing section, existing site test, and release documentation. I kept the existing release-build recipe and signature verifier as the single established build/signing path, then wrapped them with a separate uploader. This avoids duplicating Gradle setup or certificate comparison logic and keeps signing credentials on the maintainer machine.

The initial focused tests exposed two issues. A Vitest-transformed `import.meta.url` produced a Vite `/@fs/` path that Bun could not execute as a filesystem script; deriving the script path from the repository working directory fixed it. The Worker initially allowed an unrelated `/downloads/*` URL to fall through to the static asset binding; an explicit prefix 404 now keeps the public download surface limited to the two supported objects. The landing test was adjusted to expect the unpublished state, and isolated component tests cover both empty and available metadata.

## Challenges and blockers

The actual Cloudflare account credentials and maintainer signing key are intentionally unavailable in this task, and the task explicitly prohibits creating secrets, deploying, or publishing a real APK. Therefore the end-to-end R2 write and live production download were not exercised. Credential refusal paths were tested with fake values, and the Worker was tested with an in-memory bucket. Before the first real publish, the maintainer needs the configured Cloudflare token/account ID and release keystore values in their local environment or the specified config file.

A `repoos update 1296 --shots ...` attempt printed a warning that the CLI reads the canonical board from the main checkout when run inside a linked worktree. The task's worktree copy remains unchanged and no screenshot declaration was written. I stopped further RepoOS metadata commands to honor the instruction that the main checkout is off-limits. The implementation check itself completed successfully before that command.

## Key learnings

A published R2 object can remain independent of static-site deployments when the Worker only reads it through a bucket binding and the site deploy does not synchronize or clear that bucket. Keeping version metadata separate from the APK gives the landing page a cheap availability/version probe and gives users an authoritative certificate fingerprint. The metadata upload should follow the APK upload so a new version does not appear in the UI before its artifact has been sent.

The verification gate needs both checks: matching the APK signer to the configured keystore prevents a debug-signed build from passing, while inspecting the manifest's debuggable flag prevents a release-signed but debuggable artifact from being published. Missing signing and Cloudflare credentials should fail before building, and the dry-run path should retain all local verification while skipping both credentials for upload and all upload operations.

Validation completed with `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check`: remote build and scoped tests passed, followed by local format, lint, build, UI smoke, user-docs build, and landing build. Targeted tests also passed after the fixes above. No device install, live R2 operation, production deploy, or real-signing test is claimed.
